The Booster K1 is a 95 cm, 19.5 kg bipedal humanoid built for people who want to write the control code themselves.

The K1's only real competitor at this end of the market is the **Unitree G1**, and they are less alike than the price bracket suggests.
The G1 is bigger — 1.32 m, around 35 kg — with far more degrees of freedom, optional dexterous hands, and a much larger public software ecosystem.
It is also the most widely owned research humanoid in the world, which cuts both ways: the ecosystem is deeper, and on 29 August 2026 two vulnerabilities were disclosed in the G1 EDU allowing root-level remote code execution, one of them over Bluetooth.
...
No comparable audit of the K1 has been published, which is not the same as the K1 being safer.
The K1's case against it is size, price and durability.
At 95 cm and 19.5 kg it is a machine a student can carry, drop and reset alone.
It is cheaper at entry.
And it has the RoboCup evidence, which the G1 does not have in the same form.

The G1 is bigger (1.32 m, about 35 kg), has more degrees of freedom, offers dexterous hands and has the largest public software ecosystem in the category.
The K1 is smaller, cheaper at entry, easier for one person to handle, and has the stronger independent competition record.

results.snippet:
The Unitree G1 EDU and Booster K1 bring different strengths to humanoid robotics.
While the G1 EDU emphasizes configurable hardware, manipulation research and embodied AI, the K1 focuses on compact design, programmable locomotion and accessible development tools.
This comparison examines their capabilities, computing, runtime and research applications to help identify the right platform for each project.
...
The Unitree G1 EDU focuses on secondary development, flexible joint configurations, and optional dexterous hands for manipulation research.
The Booster K1 pairs a small size with programmable mobility, intelligent sensing, and a broad range of pre-installed applications.
...

|--|--|--|
|Robot type|Programmable humanoid research platform|Compact humanoid robotics development platform|
|Best-fit use cases|Humanoid locomotion, embodied AI, manipulation research and reinforcement learning|Education, soccer robotics, locomotion research and interactive development|
|Dimensions|1,320 × 450 × 200 mm (standing; H × W × D)|Approx. 950 mm standing height|
|Weight|Approx. 35 kg+ with battery|Approx. 19.5 kg|
|Degrees of freedom (DoF)|23–43, depending on configuration|22 across the head, arms and legs|
|Arm load capacity|Approx. 3 kg maximum for the EDU arm, depending on extension and posture|No directly comparable arm payload figure established in the cited specification|
|Runtime / charging|Approx. 2 h stated battery life; varies by operation and configuration|Geek: 20 min; Education/Professional: up to 70 min at the specified test speed of 1.1 m/s; charging up to 2 h|
|Navigation / sensing|Depth camera, 3D LiDAR and microphone array|Stereo/depth camera, 9-axis IMU and microphone array; perception configuration varies by edition|
|Computing|8-core CPU; optional high-compute modules, including Orin-based options|Geek: 48 TOPS; Education: 117 TOPS; Professional: 200 TOPS|
|Locomotion|Humanoid movement with configurable joint architecture and developer control|Forward/backward and lateral walking, turning, balance recovery and compound gaits|

|Distinctive capabilities|Optional three-finger force-controlled dexterous hands, additional wrist and waist axes, and extensive joint configuration|Lightweight design, built-in interactive Agents, autonomous get-up capability and an accessible development ecosystem|
|Key limitation / caveat|Confirm the exact EDU configuration, optional hands, waist joints and computing module before comparing specifications|Battery life, computing performance and warranty vary by edition; published walking-speed figures differ by test conditions|
...
Research focus and operational role: The Unitree G1 EDU is an appropriate robot for communities working on humanoid control, reinforcement learning and manipulation.
Customizable joints and optional dexterous hands expand the possibilities for experiments involving object handling and manipulation.
The Booster K1 is a robot built for embodied AI education, research in locomotion, and interactive applications with its embedded Agents supporting soccer, dance, and dialogue.
Hardware and manipulation: The G1 EDU can achieve 23-43 degrees of freedom (depending on which configuration you choose), versus 22 degrees of freedom in the K1.
But just having more degrees of freedom does not equate to better performance.
For manipulation research, the G1 EDU has optional dexterous hands, more wrist axes and a waist configuration.
The K1's light 19.5kg body makes transportation and configuration simple across classrooms, laboratories and competitions.
Computing and development: Unitree has an eight-core CPU, as well as optional high-compute modules for the G1 EDU.
Booster has three levels of its K1 with claimed AI computing capabilities of 48, 117 and 200 TOPS.
Its development environment supports Python and C++, as well as its Agent framework and simulation tools to enable a link between virtual testing and physical-robot realisation.
These figures should be weighed against access to software, supported frameworks, integration burdens and the actual computation hardware included in the purchase.
Locomotion and endurance: Both units support humanoid type walking and running, but K1 makes an explicit claim to support (horizontal) lateral walking in addition.
Booster currently states the peak walking speed on its product page as 2 m/sec and (on the spec sheet) as 1.1 m/sec under specified test conditions, and its 'Education' and 'Professional' editions are rated for 70 minutes at this specified speed compared to 20 minutes for the Geek.
Unitree lists 2 hours battery life for the G1 'EDU' model, though endurance will depend on how far it walks, what payloads it carries, what computing it uses and how it is configured - not all of these figures are directly comparable.
Deployment and usability: The K1's smaller profile and integrated interactive features could make it easier to use for demos, training and repeatable development activities.
The G1 EDU provides a more configurable research platform but its optional accessories and compute options will need to be specified carefully.
...
Booster K1: Geek, Education and Professional editions all run on the same 22-DoF body, but vary in battery and computing spec.
...
No overall performance winner for either specification sheet.
The actual test results will vary according to the task, the hardware configuration, the control software, the computer and the environment.
...
Select the Unitree G1 EDU if robotics research emphasizes customizable humanoid chassis, advanced manipulation testbeds and optional dexterous Hand development.
Select the Booster K1 if a lightweight platform, built-in interactive capabilities and a well-defined development ecosystem are the best matches for your curriculum, walking and embodiment research, and prototyping of AI working inside robots.
The choice should be driven by the needs of the research tasks, the tools provided (or not provided), software flexibility, run-time and support issues.
The best way to determine which platform will work best is to have a pilot study using the algorithms, sensors and manipulation tasks of interest.
results.title: Unitree G1 EDU vs. Booster K1

content.text:
**The Unitree G1 is the better fit for configurable research and manipulation; the Booster K1 is the better fit for a compact, lighter robot that’s easier to transport and program across its product tiers.** They’re not direct equivalents: the G1 is substantially taller and heavier, while the K1 is aimed more at education, locomotion, and interactive projects.[1][2][10]

| | Unitree G1 | Booster K1 |
|---|---|---|
| **Size** | About 132 cm and 35 kg[1] | About 95 cm and 19.5 kg[2] |
| **Degrees of freedom** | 23 on the base version; EDU configurations can offer up to 43[1] | 22[2] |
| **Programming access** | Secondary development is for EDU configurations; confirm the exact model and options[1][5] | Secondary development is listed across K1 tiers[2] |
| **Manipulation** | EDU can be configured with optional dexterous hands and additional wrist/waist joints[5][10] | Better suited to locomotion and education; no directly comparable arm-payload figure is established in the cited specs[10] |
| **Compute and runtime** | EDU options vary; roughly two hours is commonly stated, but depends on configuration and use[1][10] | Editions vary: listed compute ranges from 48 to 200 TOPS, with walking-time estimates varying by edition and test conditions[2][10] |
| **Price** | Base and EDU prices differ substantially; the base model is not equivalent to a programmable EDU robot[5][6] | Published starting prices vary by seller and configuration; get a quote for the specific tier[1][5] |

**Choose the G1 EDU** if your work needs a larger platform, optional hands, or a configurable research/manipulation setup. **Choose the K1** if portability, teaching, locomotion experiments, or programming access across tiers matter more. Compare written quotes and included hardware—not headline prices—because compute, batteries, hands, and development access depend on the exact configuration.[2][5][10]
